title: Starting on drum and cornet in the Raceland town band
summary: Older townspeople had a band and passed instruments to their sons; Miller started on bass drum, baritone, then cornet, playing marches in six-eight and Dixieland.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well, now that's the funny thing. We all, the older parents and things had a big band out there. They got a bunch of new instruments. So everyone that had a son or grandson or anything like that, well, they just give them the old instruments, see? And I don't know, I was lucky enough to come out pretty good. At first it started me on the bass drum. I started to blow in the baritone, it gave me that, I played it pretty good, so they gave me the cornet. And I took the cornet and made good history. Of course I wasn't reading music, but I played everything I could whistle.
And what about the other people in the band, the old people?
Well, the old people all died out. Were they readers? Yeah, they readers readers. The most of them. The most of them was.
Did anybody play any jazz, what you'd call jazz today in that band?
Well, it was on the same order of this.
So they were playing jazz when you were a little boy in Raceland?
Well, exactly what you called it, Dixieland, isn't it? Mm-hmm. Yeah, that's what they were playing.
And how were the people that were playing Dixieland when you were a little boy? Yeah. Have they been playing that kind of music before you think?

Well yeah, that's all I come up on it. That's all I, you know, nothing about. Until the bop come out and I started playing a little bit of that, but I was never crazy about it, you know. I just tried it out and played it. But I always did play my Dixieland.
I like it. I wondered about that. I just wondered, if those guys weren't readers they must have been playing something pretty close to Dixieland

jazz before you ever bought it. Yeah. But I'll tell you one thing about it. The most they played was like marches. See, they learned a lot of marches. They didn't know a lot of play pieces like banana peeling and all that stuff way back there, you know. Oh, you're beautiful. They played all that kind of stuff. But the most stuff they did play was marches.
Would they be six eighths or two four?
Mostly six eighths? Yeah. Well I've often wondered if you could really swing in a six eighth march.
Well I've got to slow it down a bit and cut it, cut it up you know. You've got to cut it like a whole note where you make either one half or two half notes out of it.
